newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: German, Austrian kidnap victims killed in Colombia.
newsitem.headline: German, Austrian kidnap victims killed in Colombia.

text.p: Two kidnapped foreign tourists, a German and an Austrian, were killed on Tuesday when army troops raided the guerrilla encampment in northwest Colombia where they had been held captive for nearly a month, military officials said.

Two other men, a German and an Austrian, were freed in the raid and four leftist Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) rebels were killed, Gen. Ivan Ramirez, a regional military commander, told Reuters.

He identified the dead, whom he said were killed by rebels when soldiers raided the camp in a jungle-covered area of northwestern Choco province, as Alexander Scheurer, a chef from Germany, and Johann Kehrer, a highway policeman from Austria.
Kehrer's brother, Manfred, a chemist, was rescued along with Mardean Muzinic, a builder from Germany, Ramirez said.
In a phone interview with the CM& TV news programme, Muzinic said he and Manfred Kehrer had been bathing in a river under guard when the army stormed the rebel camp.

"Of course it was the guerrillas who killed them," he replied when asked who shot his two companions to death. He said the two men that died were about 300 yards (metres) away from them when they were killed.
Muzinic said he had entered Colombia with his three friends via the remote Darien Gap, which divides the country from northern neighbour Panama.
Ramirez told Reuters the Germans and Austrians entered Colombia on Feb. 5 to visit the Los Catios nature reserve and were seized by FARC rebels.

Armed forces chief Gen. Harold Bedoya said in a radio interview that the rebels had demanded $15 million ransom for the two Germans. Other military sources said that was sum demanded for the release of all four.
German and Austrian embassy officials could not be reached for immediate comment to confirm details of the kidnap nor the circumstances in which two of the group were killed.

An army spokesman at the military base near the town of Carepa, where the survivors were spending the night, said all the tourists were aged between 25 and 30 years old but was unable to give their hometowns.
Kehrer and Muzinic were due to fly to Bogota aboard a military flight, together with the bodies of their dead companions, on Wednesday, the spokesman said.
The FARC, Colombia's largest and oldest rebel group, specialises in kidnappings and the protection of rural drug operations.
